domain: Kitchen renovation planning on a fixed budget
schema_note: Mirrors INESCTEC_RESEARCH.md section 3/4 output schema, same convention as conversations/marathon_trip. Domain entity types (domain_config.json): material, product, trade. Built to exercise numeric state that is revised repeatedly (budget SN_2, cabinets SN_3 twice, wall SN_10, start date SN_11), two decisions reverted and replaced (contractor SN_4 -> SN_5, countertop SN_6 -> SN_7), constraint: lifted (SN_13), and a late stale mention of an old value (N_41: '€18k').

schema_findings.issue: N_41 mentions the superseded €18,000 budget in passing (Miguel's phrase), without asserting it as current. It is neither a revision nor a contradiction of the current budget.
schema_findings.proposed_direction: Recorded as references to N_2 only, with no state-node link. This is the intended trap for recency-only retrieval: the most recent budget mention in the conversation carries a stale number.

schema_findings.issue: N_27 both contradicts N_14 (quartz dropped) and resolves N_26 (where to cut). One turn can close a question and overturn an earlier decision at the same time.
schema_findings.proposed_direction: Keep both pragmatic edges; they target different turns and mean different things.

schema_findings.issue: The outline's final bill (€20,950) did not add up; the corpus uses €20,050, which build.py recomputes from the line items (BUDGET) and asserts against the text.
schema_findings.proposed_direction: No schema change; recorded so the outline and corpus aren't read as inconsistent.

N_1.question: Hi! I'm Carla. My partner Miguel and I want to redo the kitchen in our Alvalade apartment. His parents are visiting in early May and we want it done before then. Where do we start?
N_1.answer: Nice project. Early May gives about four months, which is realistic for a kitchen if decisions don't drag. Start with the budget and the layout; almost everything else follows from those two.
N_1.summary: Carla and Miguel want to renovate their kitchen before early May.

N_2.question: Our total budget is €18,000, and we really can't go above it.
N_2.answer: €18,000 is workable for a mid-range kitchen in Lisbon if the layout stays mostly as it is. We'll treat it as a hard cap.

N_3.question: How is a budget like that usually split?
N_3.answer: Roughly: cabinets 25%, countertop 10–15%, labour 35–45%, appliances and tiles 15%, plus a contingency if you can. Labour is usually the biggest single line in Lisbon.
N_3.summary: Typical budget split: labour largest, cabinets ~25%, counter 10-15%.

N_4.question: For the layout, should we go L-shaped or galley?
N_4.answer: That depends on the room. What are the dimensions, and where are the window and the door?
N_4.summary: Asks about L-shaped vs galley layout.

N_5.question: The window is on the short wall and the door is opposite it, so the long back wall is free.
N_5.answer: Then an L-shape along the back wall and the window wall works well: it keeps the door path clear and gives you the most counter space.
N_5.summary: Room layout suits an L-shape along the back and window walls.

N_6.question: I measured the back wall: 3.40 m.
N_6.answer: Good; the cabinet plan will be built around 3.40 m of run on that wall.

N_7.question: IKEA or custom cabinets?
N_7.answer: With your budget, IKEA. Custom joinery for an L-shape would easily eat half the budget on its own.
N_7.summary: Asks IKEA vs custom cabinets; IKEA recommended.

N_8.question: I did the IKEA planner for Metod cabinets: €4,200 for the whole L.
N_8.answer: That's about 23% of the budget, right in range. Metod cabinets at €4,200 it is.

N_9.question: We asked two contractors for labour quotes. Ferreira Obras quoted €7,900.
N_9.answer: That's on the low end for demolition, plumbing, electrics and installation. Check what's excluded.

N_10.question: And Casa Nova Remodelações quoted €9,400, but as a fixed price, and they include waste removal.
N_10.answer: A fixed price with waste removal is worth something: fewer surprises. €1,500 more, but with a firm number.
N_10.summary: Casa Nova quotes €9,400 fixed price including waste removal.

N_11.question: Which one would you pick?
N_11.answer: On numbers alone Ferreira is cheaper. If the budget is truly tight, Ferreira, as long as the scope is written down.
N_11.summary: Assistant leans towards the cheaper Ferreira quote.

N_12.question: We'll go with Ferreira Obras then.
N_12.answer: OK, Ferreira Obras. Get the quote itemised and signed before any work starts.

N_13.question: Countertop: what material?
N_13.answer: For the look you described, quartz or a good stone-look laminate. Quartz is more durable; laminate is much cheaper.
N_13.summary: Asks about countertop material: quartz vs laminate.

N_14.question: We love quartz. The quote is €2,300 for both runs.
N_14.answer: Quartz at €2,300 is about 13% of the budget, within range. Quartz it is.

N_15.question: We want the hob on the back wall instead of by the window. That means moving the gas line. Do we need a permit?
N_15.answer: Moving a gas line is regulated work; it may need a comunicação prévia to the Câmara.
N_15.summary: Moving the hob means moving the gas line; opens whether a permit is needed.

N_16.question: How do I find out for sure?
N_16.answer: Ask the Câmara's urbanism desk or have the contractor check. Gas works also need a certified gas technician and an inspection afterwards.
N_16.summary: Check with the Câmara; gas work needs a certified technician and inspection.

N_17.question: Sr. Ferreira came to measure properly: the back wall is actually 3.28 m, not 3.40. It's out of plumb and narrower at the top.
N_17.answer: That's 12 cm less than the plan assumes, which matters for the cabinet run.
N_17.summary: Back wall re-measured at 3.28 m, out of plumb.

N_18.question: He also sent a revised quote: €2,100 extra 'for surprises', and he can only start in six weeks.
N_18.answer: An open-ended €2,100 'surprises' line on a quote you chose for being cheap removes its main advantage, and a six-week wait threatens the May deadline.
N_18.summary: Ferreira adds €2,100 for 'surprises' and a six-week wait.

N_19.question: We're not comfortable with that. Should we drop Ferreira?
N_19.answer: Yes. Ferreira at €10,000 with an open-ended line is now more expensive than Casa Nova's fixed price, and slower.

N_20.question: Then we go with Casa Nova?
N_20.answer: Yes: Casa Nova Remodelações at their €9,400 fixed price [N_10]. Ana will be your project manager.
N_20.summary: Casa Nova Remodelações hired at €9,400 fixed.

N_21.question: Ana says they can start on 2 March.
N_21.answer: 2 March leaves about eight weeks before early May, enough for a six-week job with some slack.

N_22.question: Because the wall is 3.28 m, the 40 cm drawer unit no longer fits. IKEA's planner suggests custom filler panels and a narrow custom unit. Cabinets go up to €5,100.
N_22.answer: The 12 cm shortfall forces custom pieces, so the cabinet line rises from €4,200 to €5,100.
N_22.summary: The shorter wall forces custom pieces; cabinets rise to €5,100.

N_23.question: Where does that leave the total?
N_23.answer: Cabinets €5,100 + labour €9,400 + quartz €2,300 + appliances and tiles about €2,900 = €19,700. That's €1,700 over the €18,000 cap.

N_24.question: Idea: if we switch to an induction hob, there's no gas line to move at all. Does that also get rid of the permit question?
N_24.answer: Yes. With induction there's no gas work, so there's nothing to notify the Câmara about and no gas inspection. The permit question disappears. Switching to induction solves both problems.
N_24.summary: Switch to induction: no gas work, so no permit needed.

N_25.question: Ana says induction needs a dedicated circuit, so the electrician has to upgrade it: about €650.
N_25.answer: That's a common requirement. It adds €650, so we need to keep an eye on the total.

N_26.question: So now we're at €20,350? Where can we cut?
N_26.answer: Yes, €20,350. The biggest flexible line is the countertop: a good stone-look laminate is around €800 versus €2,300 for quartz.
N_26.summary: Total €20,350; the countertop is the biggest flexible cost.

N_27.question: OK. We'll switch the countertop from quartz to the stone-look HPL laminate.
N_27.answer: That saves €1,500 and brings the total to €18,850. Still €850 over, but much closer.
N_27.summary: Countertop switched from quartz to HPL laminate; total €18,850.

N_28.question: Miguel hates the idea. He says laminate will look cheap.
N_28.answer: Modern HPL stone-look laminates are quite convincing, and they handle heat and scratches reasonably well. It's worth seeing a sample in person before deciding it looks cheap.
N_28.summary: Miguel objects to the laminate countertop.

N_29.question: News: Miguel's parents offered to help. They're adding €3,500, so our budget is now €21,500.
N_29.answer: That's very generous, and it changes the picture: the budget is now €21,500.
N_29.summary: A family top-up raises the budget to €21,500.

N_30.question: So should we go back to quartz?
N_30.answer: You could afford it now. But think about what else the margin could buy that you'd use more.
N_30.summary: Asks whether to go back to quartz given the bigger budget.

N_31.question: We talked it over. We'll keep the laminate and instead put the oven in a tall column cabinet at eye level, not under the hob. Miguel's mother has a bad back.
N_31.answer: Good use of the margin. A tall oven column adds about €900 for the cabinet and installation, and it's far more comfortable to use. Laminate stays.
N_31.summary: Keep laminate; add a tall oven column (+€900) instead of an under-hob oven.

N_32.question: Can you recap the whole budget now?
N_32.answer: Cabinets €5,100 [N_22], labour with Casa Nova €9,400 [N_20], laminate €800 [N_27], appliances and tiles €2,900, circuit upgrade €650, oven column €900 [N_31]: €19,750 against a €21,500 budget, leaving €1,750 of contingency.

N_33.question: Bad news: the porcelain tiles are delayed two weeks, so Ana moved the start to 16 March.
N_33.answer: 16 March instead of 2 March. That eats most of the slack before May.
N_33.summary: Start moved to 16 March because of a tile delay.

N_34.question: Will it still be done before the visit in early May?
N_34.answer: Let's check it against Casa Nova's schedule.
N_34.summary: Asks whether the later start still finishes before May.

N_35.question: Ana says it's a six-week job.
N_35.answer: Six weeks from 16 March ends around 27 April. Tight, but it works, provided the cabinets and tiles arrive on time.
N_35.summary: Six weeks from 16 March ends around 27 April: tight but feasible.

N_36.question: Good news: IKEA restocked a standard 30 cm Metod drawer unit. With it, the 3.28 m wall only needs a small standard filler, no custom pieces.
N_36.answer: Then drop the custom filler panels and the narrow custom unit. Cabinets come down to €4,600.
N_36.summary: A standard 30 cm unit replaces the custom pieces; cabinets €4,600.

N_37.question: Demolition started today!
N_37.answer: Exciting. The first few days usually reveal whatever is hiding behind the old cabinets.

N_38.question: They found old cloth-insulated wiring behind the back wall. Ana says it has to be replaced: €1,100.
N_38.answer: That has to be done; old cloth wiring is a fire risk. It comes out of the contingency.
N_38.summary: Old cloth wiring found; replacement costs €1,100.

N_39.question: Since the electrician is redoing the wiring anyway, does that change the induction circuit upgrade?
N_39.answer: It might; ask him to check what the hob actually needs against what's there.
N_39.summary: Asks whether the rewiring changes the induction upgrade.

N_40.question: The electrician checked: the existing 32A line to the hob position is enough for our induction hob. No upgrade needed.
N_40.answer: So the €650 circuit upgrade [N_25] is off the list; it partly offsets the rewiring.
N_40.summary: The existing 32A line suffices; the €650 upgrade is dropped.

N_41.question: Funny: Miguel told his parents on the phone that our '€18k kitchen' is coming along nicely. I didn't correct him.
N_41.answer: Ha, that number stuck from the beginning. It's a good sign that things feel on track.
N_41.summary: Miguel mentions the old '€18k' figure in passing.

N_42.question: Tiling started. Do we tile the whole wall or just the backsplash?
N_42.answer: Just the backsplash, up to the wall cabinets. Full-height tiling adds cost and time for little benefit.

N_43.question: The cabinets are being installed. The small filler at the end of the 3.28 m wall looks fine.
N_43.answer: Good; the standard filler works because the 30 cm unit absorbed most of the difference.
N_43.summary: Cabinet installation fits the 3.28 m wall.

N_44.question: The oven column is in. Miguel's mother is going to love not bending down.
N_44.answer: That was a good call. It's the change people use every single day.

N_45.question: We ran a bit short on tiles, since some broke. Ana says another box and fitting is €350.
N_45.answer: Normal breakage. €350 is fine within the remaining contingency.

N_46.question: What colour should we paint the remaining walls?
N_46.answer: A warm off-white goes well with the stone-look laminate and keeps the small room bright.
N_46.summary: Asks about wall paint colour; warm off-white suggested.

N_47.question: Ana gave us the snag list: a drawer that doesn't close fully and a missing plinth.
N_47.answer: Both are small. Make sure they're fixed before you sign off the final payment.
N_47.summary: Snag list: a drawer and a missing plinth.

N_48.question: Final bill: €20,050 in total.
N_48.answer: That matches: the €19,750 plan, minus €500 on cabinets and the €650 upgrade you didn't need, plus €1,100 rewiring and €350 tiles. €20,050 against a €21,500 budget, €1,450 under.

N_49.question: Looking back, what did we change from our original plan, and why?
N_49.answer: Four big changes. Contractor: Ferreira was dropped for an open-ended extra and a long wait [N_19], replaced by Casa Nova. Hob: induction instead of gas, which removed the permit issue [N_24]. Countertop: laminate instead of quartz to stay on budget [N_27]. Cabinets: back to a standard layout once IKEA restocked the 30 cm unit [N_36]. And the budget itself grew to €21,500.
N_49.summary: Retrospective: contractor, hob, countertop and cabinet changes.

N_50.question: Snags fixed, final payment made. The kitchen is done, two weeks before the visit!
N_50.answer: Congratulations, Carla and Miguel. Finished before the visit and under budget.
N_50.summary: Kitchen finished two weeks before the visit.

SN_1.label: Finish the kitchen before Miguel's parents visit in early May

SN_4.label: Hire Ferreira Obras as the contractor

SN_5.label: Hire Casa Nova Remodelações as the contractor (€9,400 fixed price)

SN_9.label: Switch from a gas hob to an induction hob
